Chen L, Bosmajian C, Woo S (2024). 'A highly sensitive stem-loop RT-qPCR method to study siRNA intracellular pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics.' Biology Methods & Protocols 9(1):bpae029. DOI 10.1093/biomethods/bpae029 (PMID 38783988, PMC11112049, open access; confirmed on PubMed), Supplemental Table 2 — independent lab (University at Buffalo, SUNY), uses miR-16 as the endogenous normalizer for intracellular siRNA quantification. Uses the identical Chen-2005 44-nt universal stem-loop body AND the identical 20-nt universal reverse primer as this tool; the tool's RT primer and universal reverse are byte-identical to this published set (independently re-verified against the live tool's /api/design output). SECOND, independent source for the same miRNA: Nguyen Hoang Thao Vy et al. (2020), Hoi nghi Cong nghe Sinh hoc Toan quoc 2020 (Vietnam national biotech conference proceedings, not PubMed-indexed), pp. 181-186, Table 1 — reports the same stem-loop RT primer and the same forward-primer specific region; that source's own reverse-primer entry is 19 nt ('CCAGTGCAGGGCCGAGGTA', and its own length column inconsistently says '16 bp'), an apparent transcription anomaly in that table, not used for matching here. THIRD source: Chen C et al. Nucleic Acids Res 2005;33(20):e179, DOI 10.1093/nar/gni178 (PMID 16314309), supplementary 'TaqMan miRNA assays' — RT primer GTCGTATCCAGTGCAGGGTCCGAGGTATTCGCACTGGATACGACCGCCAA, byte-identical; forward CGCGCTAGCAGCACGTAAAT.

Czimmerer Z, et al. PLoS ONE 2013;8(1):e55168. DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0055168, Table 2 (hsa-mir-155): RT GTTGGCTCTGGTGCAGGGTCCGAGGTATTCGCACCAGAGCCAACACCCCT, forward GTGGGTTAATGCTAATCGTGAT. Also Yang L-h, et al. PLoS ONE 2014;9(12):e115293. DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0115293: forward GCGGTTAATGCTAATCGTGATA (same miRNA-specific core; different USLP body). Forward-core comparison only. NOTE — overhang NOT scored: both papers anchor the RT primer on the older 23-nt mature miR-155 (3' end ...AGGGGU; Czimmerer overhang ACCCCT; Yang 8-nt ACCCCTAT), whereas miRBase v22 / this tool's database annotate hsa-miR-155-5p as 24 nt (3' end ...GGGGUU), giving overhang AACCCC. This is a reference-annotation difference, not a design error — but it means a primer ordered from the 2013/2014 papers binds a 1-nt-shifted 3' end.

Yang L-h, et al. Universal Stem-Loop Primer Method. PLoS ONE 2014;9(12):e115293. DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0115293 — miR-150 forward qPCR primer (5' GC tail added to raise Tm). NOTE: Yang 2014 uses a different stem-loop body and reverse (random 3' end), so only the forward miRNA-specific core is comparable; no RT exact-match applies. Yang's miR-150 stem-loop 3' end is CACTGGTA (8 nt binding); this tool's 6-nt overhang CACTGG is its prefix — within Chen's 6-8 nt range, not scored.

Czimmerer Z, et al. A Versatile Method to Design Stem-Loop Primer-Based Quantitative PCR Assays. PLoS ONE 2013;8(1):e55168. NOTE: different universal body (GTTGGCTCTGG...CCAGAGCCAAC) and reverse (GTGCAGGGTCCGAGGT), so no full-RT exact-match applies — only the 6-nt overhang and the forward miRNA-specific core are comparable.

Ngo Thi Mai Vy (student ID 20187223). 'Development of the Quantification Procedure for miR-125b-5p in Human Plasma Samples Using Stemloop RT-qPCR.' Bachelor's thesis (lab internal, unpublished). Same Chen-2005 universal stem-loop body; universal reverse GCAGGGTCCGAGGTATTC (18 nt, a different loop window than this tool's fixed 20-nt reverse, so reverse is not exact-matched). RT overhang TCACAA = revcomp of 3'-terminal UUGUGA (independently verified).

Zhao F-L, Dou Y-C, Wang X-F, Han D-C, Lv Z-G, Ge S-L, Zhang Y-K. 'Serum microRNA-195 is down-regulated in breast cancer: a potential marker for the diagnosis of breast cancer.' Mol Biol Rep. 2014;41(9):5913-5922. DOI 10.1007/s11033-014-3466-1, Table 2 ('The sequences of miR-16 and miR-195 stem-loop RT and PCR primers'). Same Chen-2005 universal stem-loop body (GTCGTATCCAGTGCAGGGTCCGAGGTATTCGCACTGGATACGAC) and universal reverse GCAGGGTCCGAGGTATTC. NOTE: the published RT hybridizes 7 nt (GCCAATA = revcomp of 3'-terminal UAUUGGC); this tool's fixed 6-nt overhang (GCCAAT) is the 6-nt prefix of it — a deliberate design choice within Chen's 6-8 nt binding range, not a mismatch. Forward-specific core comparison only.

Forward-specific core comparison only (stem-loop 3' overhang in the source table was not machine-legible).

Varkonyi-Gasic E, Wu R, Wood M, Walton EF, Hellens RP. 'Protocol: a highly sensitive RT-PCR method for detection and quantification of microRNAs.' Plant Methods 2007;3:12. DOI 10.1186/1746-4811-3-12 (PMID 17931426, PMC2225395; confirmed on PubMed), Table 1. Same 44-nt stem-loop body as this tool; universal reverse is the 16-nt GTGCAGGGTCCGAGGT (sub-window of this tool's 20-nt reverse, not exact-matched). The paper lists the mature sequence without a species prefix; it is identical to the Arabidopsis entry named here (the sequence is conserved across many plant species in miRBase). PLANT miRNA: outside the tool's specificity data (family/overhang-collision index is hsa/mmu/rno, BLAST is human cDNA) — only primer design is validated.
